messages:
maya: Heads up — 9h layover in Munich next week. Thinking about buying a day-pass for the lounge to get some focused work done. Anyone tried lounge day-passes recently (MUC/CDG/LHR)? Worth it vs coffee shops / airport coworking? @sam

sam: I used Plaza Premium at MUC last month. Day pass ~€30, decent Wi‑Fi but spots are limited during peak. Bring a dongle for power. :coffee:

joel: If you need real desks, check LoungeBuddy or the airport app — some lounges have dedicated work rooms. I once found a quiet corner with a proper desk at MUC Terminal 2.

zara: CDG is hit-or-miss. Priority Pass gets you into smaller lounges which are crowded. For long layovers I prefer a paid co‑working day pass (Regus / WeWork near airports) — quieter and better internet.

maya: thanks! How about power outlets? My laptop is USB‑C only.

leo: USB‑C PD is fine in most lounges but bring a short USB‑C to C cable and a little 65W charger. Some lounges have plenty of outlets, others only near the buffet. Also pack a tiny power strip if you want extra ports.

sam: Pro tip — screenshot the lounge entry rules and opening hours. Some have weird midday closures. Also check boarding-pass gating; some lounges only admit same‑day confirmed flights.

zara: If you want privacy, book a nap pod or "minute suites" if available. Not cheap but great for jetlag + a few hours of deep work.

joel: One weird thing — CDG wifi occasionally blocks Zoom. VPN helps. Also avoid the buffet area if you need quiet. :grimacing: 

maya: Any quick recs for best quiet lounges at MUC? Low noise, good desks?

leo: I'll DM you a short list (MUC T1: Lufthansa Senator has a business corner; T2: some lounges open with workspaces), but double-check access rules. ping @maya :white_check_mark:

airportbot: Flight FR123 to BCN delayed 30m — lounge members may be offered discounted access at the gate.

maya: awesome, thanks everyone. Saving notes. :raised_hands:
